Rashi on Keritot 19b:1:1.hebrew: מתעסק בחלבים - כגון חלב ושומן לפניו, ונודע שזה חלב וזה שומן, ונתכוון לאכול שומן, והביט למקום אחר, והלכה ידו אל החלב ואכלו. אי נמי, חלב וחלב לפניו, וסבור שהוא שומן, ונתכוין לאכול חתיכה זו, ואכל את זו. ולא דמי לשוגג, דשוגג היינו שנתכוין לחתיכה זו עצמה, אבל סבור שהוא שומן:
Rashi on Keritot 19b:1:1.english: Acts unawares with regard to forbidden fats - For example, forbidden fat and permitted fat [were] before him, and it was known [to him] that this is forbidden fat and that is permitted fat, and he intended to eat permitted fat, but looked elsewhere, and his hand went to the forbidden fat and he ate it. Alternatively, [two pieces of] forbidden fat [were] before him, and he thought that it was permitted fat, and he intended to eat this piece, yet he ate that one. And [this] is not similar to an unwitting transgressor, for an unwitting transgressor is [one] who intended [to eat] this very piece itself, but thought that it was permitted fat.

Rashi on Keritot 19b:1:2.hebrew: מתעסק בעריות - כגון נתכוון לבוא על אשתו נדה וסבור טהורה היא, או אחותו ואשתו לפניו, ונשמטה אשתו ולא ידע, ובאה אחותו במקומה. ולא דמי לשוגג, דשוגג כגון שנתכוון לזו עצמה וסבור שהיא אשתו:
Rashi on Keritot 19b:1:2.english: One who acts unawares with those with whom intercourse is forbidden - For example, he intended to cohabit with his wife [who was] a menstruant [niddah] and thought she was pure; [or] his sister and his wife were before him, and his wife slipped away and he did not know, and his sister came in her place. And this is not similar to an unwitting transgressor [shogeg], for an unwitting transgressor [is], for example, one who intended [to cohabit] with this [woman] herself and thought that she was his wife.

Rashi on Keritot 19b:2:1.english: Rather, [it refers to] one who acts unawares on Shabbat - [It is] for this that the verse comes to exempt him. [The case of] one who acts unawares on Shabbat [the Gemara] explains further on.

Rashi on Keritot 19b:2:2.english: Planned labor - That he planned and intended this very labor.

Rashi on Keritot 19b:3:1.hebrew: משכחת לה - מתעסק בשבת, כגון שנתכוון כו':
Rashi on Keritot 19b:3:1.english: You find it - [The case of one] acting unawares on Shabbat, "such as where [one] intended," etc.

Rashi on Keritot 19b:3:2.hebrew: להגביה - פטור לדברי הכל, דהאי מתעסק הוי, דלא נתכוון לשום חתיכה:
Rashi on Keritot 19b:3:2.english: To lift - He is exempt according to all [opinions], for this is [a case of] acting unawares, as he did not intend any cutting.

Tosafot on Keritot 19b:4:1.hebrew: לשון התוספות דאיתמר נתכוין להגביה התלוש וחתך המחובר - לפי מה שפירשנו, צריך לומר: "ועלה בידו מחובר", אותו עצמו שנתכוון לו; דאי חתך מחובר אחר, אמאי נקט "נתכוון לתלוש"? אפי' נתכוין למחובר פטור, כמו ההיא דשתי נרות, ונתכוון לכבות את זו וכיבה את זו. ורבינו שלמה יצחקי לא פירש כן:
Tosafot on Keritot 19b:4:1.english: The text of Tosafot: "As it was stated: [If] one intended to lift the detached [plant] and cut the attached [plant]" - According to what we explained [earlier], one must say [that the case is where] "an attached [plant] came up in his hand" — [meaning] that very same [plant] that he intended [to lift or cut]. For if he cut a different attached [plant], why did [the Gemara] state "he intended [to cut] a detached [plant]"? Even if he intended [to cut] an attached [plant, and mistakenly cut a different attached plant], he would be exempt, like that [case] of two candles where he intended to extinguish this one and extinguished that one. However, Rabbeinu Shlomo Yitzchaki [Rashi] did not explain it this way.

Tosafot on Keritot 19b:4:2.hebrew: דהא לא איכוון לחתיכה דאיסורא - ואם תאמר: שוגג נמי דכל התורה כולה לא מתכוון לאיסור? ויש לומר: בכל התורה כולה, כשאמר מותר, הוא בשוגג בדבר שהוא ידוע לנו שהוא איסור; אבל הכא מתכוון לדבר שהוא היתר לכולי עלמא אם היה כפי מה שהוא סבור, ולכך פטור משום דהוי מתעסק:
Tosafot on Keritot 19b:4:2.english: For he did not intend [to perform] a prohibited cutting - And if you ask: An unwitting transgressor throughout the entire Torah also does not intend [to commit] a prohibition! One can answer: Throughout the entire Torah, when he says "It is permitted," he is acting unwittingly regarding something that is known to us to be a prohibition; however, here he intends [to do] something that is permitted according to everyone if it were as he assumes, and therefore he is exempt because he is [considered] acting unawares (mit'asek).
